Step 4: Fluoroalkanes do not undergo E1 elimination because primary/secondary carbocations are not formed spontaneously from fluoride departure without strong Lewis acid assistance. Thus statement D is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The directing and activating effects of halomethyl groups on the benzene ring differ dramatically between chloromethylbenzene ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$) and (trichloromethyl)benzene ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CCl}_3$). Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding their electrophilic aromatic substitutions?
options: A) (Trichloromethyl)benzene undergoes electrophilic nitration predominantly at the meta-position because the three strongly electronegative chlorine atoms exert a potent $-I$ inductive effect that destabilizes ortho and para arenium ions.
B) Chloromethylbenzene undergoes electrophilic bromination predominantly at the meta-position because chlorine is a deactivating substituent.
C) In (trichloromethyl)benzene, the $-\text{CCl}_3$ group donates electron density into the ring through $+M$ resonance via chlorine lone pair overlap with the $\pi$-system.

D) In (trichloromethyl)benzene, negative (reverse) hyperconjugation delocalizes benzene $\pi$-electron density into the vacant $\sigma^*_{\text{C}-\text{Cl}}$ antibonding orbitals, further deactivating the ortho and para positions toward electrophilic attack.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: In (trichloromethyl)benzene ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CCl}_3$), the central carbon is bonded to three electronegative chlorine atoms, creating a large partial positive charge on carbon ($\text{C}^{\delta+}$). This exerts an intense $-I$ inductive electron withdrawal from the attached benzene carbon, confirming statement A.
Step 2: In chloromethylbenzene ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$), the $-\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$ group retains two $\text{C}-\text{H}$ bonds capable of normal $\sigma \to \pi$ hyperconjugation. The inductive deactivation by a single chlorine is weak. Electrophilic attack occurs preferentially at the ortho and para positions (ortho/para-directing). Thus statement B is false.
Step 3: The chlorine atoms in $-\text{CCl}_3$ are attached to an $sp^3$ carbon, so their lone pairs are not directly conjugated with the aromatic $\pi$-system, ruling out any $+M$ donation. Thus statement C is false.
Step 4: Reverse (negative) hyperconjugation involves donation of electron density from the aromatic $\pi$-system into the low-lying $\sigma^*_{\text{C}-\text{Cl}}$ antibonding orbitals ($\pi \to \sigma^*_{\text{C}-\text{Cl}}$). This interaction removes electron density preferentially from the ortho and para positions, rendering $-\text{CCl}_3$ strongly deactivating and meta-directing, validating statement D.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The solvolytic behavior of 2-norbornyl sulfonate esters exemplifies neighbouring group participation (anchimeric assistance) by carbon-carbon $\sigma$-bonds. Consider the acetolysis of optically active exo-2-norbornyl brosylate and endo-2-norbornyl brosylate in acetic acid. Which of the following statements is/are correct?
options: A) Exo-2-norbornyl brosylate undergoes acetolysis approximately 350 times faster than endo-2-norbornyl brosylate due to anchimeric assistance by the C1-C6 $\sigma$-bond.
B) Acetolysis of enantiomerically pure exo-2-norbornyl brosylate yields completely racemic exo-2-norbornyl acetate ($100\%$ loss of optical activity).
C) Endo-2-norbornyl brosylate reacts with direct backside assistance by the C1-C6 $\sigma$-bond to give pure endo-2-norbornyl acetate.
D) The intermediate formed during exo-brosylate ionization is a symmetrical, meso non-classical carbocation possessing a two-electron, three-center (2e-3c) bond delocalized over C-1, C-2, and C-6.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: In exo-2-norbornyl brosylate, the departing brosylate group ($-OBs$) is anti-periplanar to the C1-C6 $\sigma$-bonding orbital. As $-OBs$ departs, the C1-C6 $\sigma$-bond electrons participate from the backside in a concerted ionization (anchimeric assistance), drastically lowering the activation energy and accelerating the solvolysis rate by a factor of $\sim 350$ relative to the endo isomer, confirming statement A.
Step 2: This assisted ionization generates the bridged, non-classical 2-norbornyl cation. In this intermediate, the positive charge and bonding pair are delocalized across a three-center two-electron (2e-3c) bond involving C-1, C-2, and C-6. This bridged cation has a plane of symmetry passing through C-4, C-5, C-6, and the midpoint of the C1-C2 bond, making it an achiral (meso) species, validating statement D.
Step 3: Because the non-classical cation is meso, nucleophilic attack of acetic acid from the exo face at C-2 and C-1 occurs with equal 50% probability. Attack at C-2 yields $(1R,2S,4S)$-exo-acetate, while attack at C-1 yields $(1S,2R,4R)$-exo-acetate. These two products are non-superimposable mirror images formed in equimolar amounts, resulting in complete racemization ($0\%$ optical activity), validating statement B.
Step 4: In endo-2-norbornyl brosylate, the leaving group is cis to the C1-C6 $\sigma$-bond, precluding backside $\sigma$-participation. It ionizes unassisted at a much slower rate to an initial classical ion pair, which then leaks into the non-classical ion to give predominantly exo-acetate. Thus statement C is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: When 1-chloro-3-methylbenzene (meta-chlorotoluene) is treated with potassium amide in liquid ammonia ($\text{KNH}_2 / \text{liquid } \text{NH}_3$), dehydrohalogenation generates two distinct isomeric benzyne intermediates. Subsequent nucleophilic addition of amide ion produces all possible isomeric toluidines (ortho-, meta-, and para-toluidines). Calculate the total number of constitutionally isomeric toluidines formed in this reaction.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: In 1-chloro-3-methylbenzene, the chlorine atom is at C-1 and the methyl group is at C-3. The substrate possesses two distinct protons adjacent to the chlorine: one at C-2 (flanked between $-\text{Cl}$ and $-\text{CH}_3$) and one at C-6.
Step 2: Deprotonation by amide ion at C-2 followed by loss of chloride generates the 3-methyl-1,2-dehydrobenzene intermediate (2,3-dehydrotoluene). Deprotonation at C-6 generates the 4-methyl-1,2-dehydrobenzene intermediate (3,4-dehydrotoluene).
Step 3: In the nucleophilic addition step:
- Addition of $\text{NH}_2^-$ to 2,3-dehydrotoluene can occur at C-2 to give 2-methylaniline (ortho-toluidine) or at C-3 (accompanied by protonation) to give 3-methylaniline (meta-toluidine).
- Addition of $\text{NH}_2^-$ to 3,4-dehydrotoluene can occur at C-3 to give 3-methylaniline (meta-toluidine) or at C-4 to give 4-methylaniline (para-toluidine).
Step 4: Combining the products: ortho-toluidine, meta-toluidine, and para-toluidine are all formed. Therefore, the total number of constitutionally isomeric toluidine products is 3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: When 1-chloro-2-methylpropane (isobutyl chloride) is heated with alcoholic potassium hydroxide ($\text{alc. KOH}$), an E2 elimination takes place yielding alkene $\text{M}$ as the sole organic elimination product. Calculate the total number of hyperconjugative $\alpha$-hydrogens present in alkene $\text{M}$.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: In 1-chloro-2-methylpropane, $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$, there is only one $\beta$-carbon (C-2), which bears a single tertiary $\beta$-hydrogen.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Photochemical monochlorination of methylcyclobutane with molecular chlorine ($Cl_2 / h\nu$) produces a complex mixture of constitutional and stereoisomeric monochloro derivatives. Calculate the total number of stereoisomers (counting all pairs of enantiomers and diastereomers) present in the complete monochlorination product mixture.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Identify all constitutional positions for radical monochlorination on methylcyclobutane, and determine the number of stereoisomers for each constitutional isomer:
Step 2: Substitution at C-1 (tertiary carbon): Yields 1-chloro-1-methylcyclobutane. The cyclobutane ring has a vertical plane of symmetry passing through C-1 and C-3. The molecule has no chiral centers and cannot exhibit cis-trans isomerism. Total stereoisomers = 1.
Step 3: Substitution at C-2 (secondary carbon): Yields 1-chloro-2-methylcyclobutane. Both C-1 and C-2 are chiral stereocenters with four distinct groups. This constitutional isomer gives cis and trans diastereomers:
- Cis-1-chloro-2-methylcyclobutane is chiral and exists as a pair of enantiomers: $(1R, 2S)$ and $(1S, 2R)$ (2 stereoisomers).
- Trans-1-chloro-2-methylcyclobutane is chiral and exists as a pair of enantiomers: $(1R, 2R)$ and $(1S, 2S)$ (2 stereoisomers).
Total from C-2 substitution = $2 + 2 = 4$ stereoisomers.
Step 4: Substitution at C-3 (secondary carbon opposite methyl): Yields 1-chloro-3-methylcyclobutane. A plane of symmetry bisects C-1 and C-3, so neither isomer has chiral centers, but they exhibit geometric isomerism:
- Cis-1-chloro-3-methylcyclobutane (meso/achiral, 1 isomer).
- Trans-1-chloro-3-methylcyclobutane (achiral, 1 isomer).
Total from C-3 substitution = 2 stereoisomers.
Step 5: Substitution at the methyl group: Yields (chloromethyl)cyclobutane. The ring is symmetrical and C-1 is not a stereocenter. Total stereoisomers = 1.
Step 6: Summing all stereoisomers across all constitutional positions: $1 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 8$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A $0.10\text{ M}$ solution of enantiomerically pure $(2R)$-2-bromooctane is reacted with $1.0\text{ M}$ sodium ethoxide in absolute ethanol at $50^\circ\text{C}$. The reaction consumes substrate via parallel bimolecular pathways with total second-order rate constant $k_{\text{tot}} = 3.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ M}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}$. Quantitative kinetic analysis reveals that bimolecular elimination (E2) accounts for $60\%$ of the consumed substrate, while bimolecular substitution ($S_N2$) accounts for $40\%$. Unimolecular dissociation ($S_N1/E1$) is completely negligible. What is the stereochemical configuration and mole percentage of $(2S)$-2-ethoxyoctane in the total organic reaction products (alkenes + ethers)?
options: A) 20 mole percent $(2S)$-2-ethoxyoctane, accompanied by 20 mole percent $(2R)$-2-ethoxyoctane due to partial racemization
B) 40 mole percent pure $(2S)$-2-ethoxyoctane formed with complete stereochemical Walden inversion
C) 60 mole percent pure $(2S)$-2-ethoxyoctane because ethoxide acts primarily as a nucleophile
D) 100 mole percent $(2S)$-2-ethoxyoctane because elimination products are volatile and escape from solution
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Set up the product mole balance from the given kinetic branching data. The substrate $(2R)$-2-bromooctane reacts exclusively via bimolecular pathways: Rate$_{\text{tot}} = \text{Rate}_{E2} + \text{Rate}_{SN2}$. The branching ratio indicates that $60\%$ of the consumed alkyl halide is converted to octene elimination products (oct-1-ene, $(E)$-oct-2-ene, and $(Z)$-oct-2-ene), while $40\%$ is converted to substitution products (ethoxyoctane ethers).
Step 2: Analyze the stereochemistry of the substitution pathway. Under bimolecular $S_N2$ conditions with a powerful unhindered nucleophile ($\text{EtO}^-$) in concentrated solution, substitution proceeds with $100\%$ stereospecific backside inversion (Walden inversion). No planar carbocation is formed, precluding racemization.
Step 3: Assign the stereocenter: backside attack of ethoxide on $(2R)$-2-bromooctane yields $(2S)$-2-ethoxyoctane with complete inversion of configuration. Because $S_N2$ accounts for $40\%$ of the total consumed substrate, $(2S)$-2-ethoxyoctane constitutes exactly 40 mole percent of the total organic reaction products.
Proposing 20 mole percent of each enantiomer erroneously assumes carbocation-mediated racemization. Proposing 60 mole percent confuses the substitution yield with the elimination yield.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: When enantiomerically pure $(2R,3R)$-3-bromobutan-2-ol is treated with concentrated hydrobromic acid ($HBr$), substitution of the hydroxyl group by bromine occurs with anchimeric assistance (neighbouring group participation) from the adjacent bromine atom via a cyclic bromonium ion intermediate. Calculate the total number of enantiomers present in the resulting stereoisomeric mixture of 2,3-dibromobutane.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Protonation of the hydroxyl group in $(2R,3R)$-3-bromobutan-2-ol produces an oxonium leaving group ($-\text{OH}_2^+$) at C-2.
Step 2: The bromine atom at C-3 acts as an internal nucleophile, attacking C-2 from the backside with simultaneous expulsion of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ (anchimeric assistance). This backside attack inverts the configuration at C-2 from $(R)$ to $(S)$, forming a bridged, cyclic three-membered bromonium ion intermediate.
Step 3: Examine the symmetry of the bromonium ion derived from the $(2R,3R)$ precursor. In this bridged ion, the methyl groups are trans to each other across the three-membered ring; the intermediate possesses $C_2$ rotational symmetry and is chiral (trans-bromonium ion).
Step 4: The incoming bromide ion ($\text{Br}^-$) attacks either C-2 or C-3 from the face opposite the bridged bromine with equal probability (50% each):
- Attack at C-2 causes a second inversion at C-2, returning it to $(R)$ while C-3 retains $(R)$, yielding $(2R,3R)$-2,3-dibromobutane.
- Attack at C-3 inverts C-3 from $(R)$ to $(S)$ while C-2 remains $(S)$, yielding $(2S,3S)$-2,3-dibromobutane.
Step 5: The two products are non-superimposable mirror images formed in exactly equal amounts (an equimolar racemic mixture of $(2R,3R)$- and $(2S,3S)$-2,3-dibromobutane). Therefore, exactly 2 enantiomers are present in the product mixture.
